options.text: Aspirin 100 mg orally daily commenced now, continued throughout pregnancy
Aspirin 100 mg orally daily plus prophylactic-dose enoxaparin 40 mg subcutaneously daily, continued throughout pregnancy and 6 weeks postpartum
Therapeutic-dose enoxaparin 1 mg/kg subcutaneously twice daily and warfarin to INR 2 to 3 after the first trimester
Hydroxychloroquine 200 mg twice daily as monotherapy throughout pregnancy
Prednisolone 20 mg orally daily plus IVIG infusion 1 g/kg monthly

subtopic_detail: Polyarteritis nodosa - hepatitis B association and treatment
stem:
A 47-year-old man presents to your hospital clinic with 8 weeks of weight loss (8 kg), fevers, severe testicular pain, livedo reticularis on the lower limbs, hypertension (BP 178/108) and a new right foot drop. He emigrated from Vietnam 20 years ago. Bloods show haemoglobin 102, WCC 13.4, platelets 488, creatinine 138 (baseline 80), ALT 142, AST 168, GGT 240, ALP 168, albumin 32, CRP 96.

Hepatitis B surface antigen is positive, HBeAg positive, HBV DNA 4.6 x10^7 IU/mL, anti-HCV negative, HIV negative, ANCA negative (both PR3 and MPO), ANA negative, cryoglobulins negative, complement normal. Urinalysis shows no blood, no protein. Mesenteric angiography demonstrates multiple small renal and mesenteric arterial microaneurysms; renal biopsy is deferred given imaging findings.

data_table.Vital signs: BP 178/108, HR 96, afebrile today.
data_table.Examination: Livedo reticularis lower limbs, right foot drop, testicular tenderness.
data_table.Bloods: Hb 102, WCC 13.4, plt 488, creatinine 138 (baseline 80), ALT 142, AST 168, GGT 240, ALP 168, albumin 32, CRP 96.
data_table.Serology: HBsAg+, HBeAg+, HBV DNA 4.6x10^7 IU/mL, anti-HCV neg, HIV neg, ANCA neg, ANA neg, cryoglobulins neg.
data_table.Imaging: Mesenteric angio: multiple renal and mesenteric microaneurysms.

lead_in: Which is the single most appropriate treatment combination?

options.text: Prednisolone 1 mg/kg/day plus cyclophosphamide 2 mg/kg/day orally for 12 months
Short course of high-dose corticosteroid (e.g. prednisolone 1 mg/kg tapered over 2 weeks) plus plasma exchange, plus immediate antiviral therapy with entecavir or tenofovir
Rituximab 375 mg/m2 weekly for 4 weeks plus prednisolone 1 mg/kg/day
Pegylated interferon-alpha monotherapy for 48 weeks with prednisolone 60 mg daily
Prednisolone 1 mg/kg/day monotherapy with antihypertensive optimisation, deferring antiviral until vasculitis resolves

stem: A 68-year-old man presents with 2 days of productive cough, fevers, and rigors. He has type 2 diabetes and COPD. He appears unwell with mottled periphery and delayed capillary refill but is alert and oriented.

data_table.Vital signs: BP 84/52 mmHg, HR 118 bpm, RR 26 bpm, temperature 39.4 degrees C, SpO2 91% RA
data_table.Investigations: WCC 18.2 x10^9/L, CRP 286 mg/L, lactate 4.8 mmol/L, creatinine 162 micromol/L (baseline 88), glucose 14.2 mmol/L

lead_in: Which hour-1 bundle component has the strongest evidence for mortality reduction?

options.text: Measurement of serum lactate for risk stratification and resuscitation guidance
Administration of broad-spectrum antibiotics within 1 hour of sepsis recognition
Rapid administration of 30 mL/kg crystalloid for hypotension or lactate above 4
Blood culture collection before antibiotic administration to guide de-escalation
Vasopressor initiation targeting MAP above 65 mmHg during or after fluid resuscitation

stem: A 72-year-old woman is being resuscitated for septic shock secondary to pyelonephritis. She has received 2 litres of IV saline, commenced piperacillin-tazobactam, and noradrenaline started. MAP is now 68 mmHg. Initial lactate was 5.2 mmol/L.

data_table.Vital signs: BP 92/58 mmHg (MAP 68), HR 104 bpm, RR 22 bpm, temperature 38.8 degrees C, SpO2 96% on 4L NP, urine output 15 mL/hr
data_table.Investigations: Repeat lactate (2 hours later): 4.8 mmol/L

lead_in: What does the repeat lactate indicate and what is the appropriate response?

options.text: Resuscitation is adequate as MAP exceeds 65 mmHg and no further action is needed
The elevated lactate is likely type B from catecholamine infusion, not reflecting perfusion
Lactate clearance is inadequate - intensify resuscitation and reassess at 2-4 hours
Sodium bicarbonate should be administered to treat the lactic acidosis directly
Lactate monitoring is unreliable once vasopressors commenced and should be replaced

stem: A 58-year-old man with poorly controlled hypertension presents with BP 214/126 mmHg and headache since this morning. He is alert with no focal neurological deficits. Fundoscopy shows AV nipping and copper wiring but no haemorrhages or papilloedema. Urine dipstick negative. ECG shows LVH. Creatinine 118 micromol/L (baseline 112). CT brain normal.

data_table.Vital signs: BP 214/126 mmHg bilateral, HR 86 bpm, RR 16 bpm
data_table.Investigations: ECG: LVH, no ST changes. Creatinine 118 (baseline 112). Urine negative. Troponin <5 ng/L. CT brain: no acute pathology
data_table.Examination: GCS 15, no focal deficit, grade II hypertensive retinopathy

lead_in: What is the most appropriate classification and management?

options.text: Hypertensive emergency requiring IV labetalol infusion and ICU admission now
Hypertensive urgency with oral therapy and gradual reduction over 24-48 hours
Malignant hypertension given grade II retinopathy requiring urgent parenteral treatment
Hypertensive urgency with oral therapy optimisation and BP reduction over days to weeks
Hypertensive emergency due to headache requiring immediate IV sodium nitroprusside

stem: A 52-year-old man presents with sudden severe tearing chest pain radiating to his back. He has poorly controlled hypertension. BP is 228/132 mmHg right arm and 186/108 mmHg left arm. He is diaphoretic. CT aortogram confirms Stanford type B dissection from left subclavian to renal arteries without malperfusion.

data_table.Vital signs: Right arm BP 228/132, Left arm BP 186/108, HR 108 bpm, RR 22 bpm
data_table.Investigations: CT aortogram: Stanford type B dissection, no malperfusion. Creatinine 94 micromol/L, troponin 18 ng/L

lead_in: What is the most appropriate initial IV antihypertensive and target?

options.text: IV sodium nitroprusside infusion titrated to systolic BP below 120 within 30 minutes
IV hydralazine boluses targeting systolic BP below 160 mmHg within 1 hour
IV GTN infusion targeting resolution of chest pain as the primary treatment endpoint
IV esmolol infusion targeting HR below 60 then adding nitroprusside for residual BP
IV labetalol infusion targeting systolic BP 100-120 mmHg and HR below 60 within 20 min
